evidence.description: The workflow collapses each plot's repeated visits into a single baseline value and a single follow-up mean before any test is applied, so each plot contributes exactly one record.
evidence.observed_value: collapse_to_plots produces one (plot, baseline, follow-up mean, count) tuple per plot

source_refs.quoted_text:
def collapse_to_plots(visits):
    """Reduce each plot to (plot_id, baseline, follow-up mean, follow-up count)."""
    records = []
    for plot in sorted(visits):
        by_session = visits[plot]
        baseline = by_session[BASELINE_LABEL]
        follow_ups = [v for label, v in by_session.items() if label != BASELINE_LABEL]
        if not follow_ups:
            raise ValueError("plot %s has no follow-up visit" % plot)
        records.append((plot, baseline, statistics.fmean(follow_ups), len(follow_ups)))
    return records

evidence.description: The Wilcoxon signed-rank test is called on the per-plot baseline and follow-up-mean lists derived from the collapsed records, i.e., 12 paired values, not on the 48 raw rows.

source_refs.quoted_text:
visits, n_rows = read_visits(INPUT_PATH)
    records = collapse_to_plots(visits)
    baselines = [rec[1] for rec in records]
    finals = [rec[2] for rec in records]

    outcome = wilcoxon(finals, baselines, alternative="two-sided")

A row-level analysis of 48 or 36 rows would not produce these values.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to show the issue is present by tracing every path from the 48-row input to the test. read_visits ingests all 48 rows but stores them keyed by plot and session; collapse_to_plots reduces each plot to one baseline and one follow-up mean; main() calls wilcoxon on the resulting 12-element finals and baselines lists, so no plot enters the test more than once. I checked for duplicate (plot_id, session_label) rows that could distort the collapse (none exist; every plot has exactly one baseline and three follow-ups). I then tested whether the reported statistics could instead reflect a row-level analysis: with n = 12 and all 12 changes positive, W = 0 and the exact two-sided p = 2/2^12 = 0.000488 exactly match the report; a test on 36 follow-up rows or 48 rows would yield a different n and a far smaller p, and the report explicitly states n = 12 plots. I also recomputed the plot-level table (e.g., PLT-01 follow-up mean 51.0, mean baseline 583/12 = 48.6) and it matches. All falsification attempts failed, supporting the verdict that the independent unit enters the row-independent procedure exactly once.
